Thus this is an ACTUAL QLS10. The10 qubit rays are distinct because z_a/z_a' is never+/-1 for a!=a'. The10 second-factor rays are distinct because w is not a character times a constant. all_resolution_obstruction_proof: Suppose any transversal were an ONB. It selects exactly two rows (epsilon=0,1) for each a. Qubit rays from different a are NEVER orthogonal, so the corresponding spans of their selected second-factor vectors must be pairwise orthogonal in C5.
Five nonzero second-factor spans in C5 force EACH span to be exactly one-dimensional. Thus the two selected second-factor rays for a fixed a must be parallel.

If their eta are equal, orthonormality within that V basis forces equal k=a+b, hence equal b, so the same COLUMN was selected twice: not a transversal. If their eta differ, epsilon+eta is the SAME for the two rows; the qubit rays are then parallel too, making the two full vectors parallel rather than orthogonal. Both possibilities fail.

This proof retains arbitrary second-factor bases; it does not rely on generic cross-basis overlaps, an odd-count shortcut, or selected transversals. It excludes every possible transversal/resolution for the stated family.
